title: OpenXRInterface never emits play_area_changed
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in v4.5.1.stable.official [f62fdbde1]

### System information

Godot v4.5.1.stable - Windows 11 (build 26100) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2060 SUPER (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.7683) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-10700 CPU @ 2.90GHz (16 threads) - 63.67 GiB memory

### Issue description

The intent of `XRInterface.play_area_changed` is documented in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/49942:

> Finally a signal `play_area_changed` is introduced that should be emitted whenever the play area changes regardless of the cause of this change. It is up to the XR interface to emit this signal, the signal definition is purely there for standardization.

But this is not implemented. `play_area_changed` is only mentioned 3 times in the entire codebase:
```
wb4@laptop:~/Downloads/godot-master$ grep -r play_area_changed *
doc/classes/XRInterface.xml:            <signal name="play_area_changed">
servers/xr/xr_interface.cpp:    ADD_SIGNAL(MethodInfo("play_area_changed", PropertyInfo(Variant::INT, "mode")));
servers/xr/xr_interface.cpp:    // `play_area_changed` should be emitted if play area data is available and either the reference frame or world scale changes.
wb4@laptop:~/Downloads/godot-master$
```

There is supposed to be code in `modules/openxr/openxr_interface.cpp` to emit this signal when appropriate.


### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a basic OpenXR project.
2. Create a new script described in the following steps and attach it to a node.
  a. Find the `"OpenXR"` interface from the `XRServer`.
  b. Connect its `play_area_changed` signal to a method that prints a message to the console.
3. Remote Deploy the project to a Quest 3.
4. While it is running, change the roomscale guardian.
5. Observe that the message never gets printed to the Godot Output console.

```
extends Node

func _ready() -> void:
	var xr_interface := XRServer.find_interface("OpenXR")
	xr_interface.play_area_changed.connect(_on_play_area_changed)

func _on_play_area_changed(mode: int) -> void:
	print("Play area changed.  mode = " + str(mode))
```

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[BasicVR.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/23279657/BasicVR.zip)

I had to delete the Android Build Template and the Godot OpenXR Vendors plugin to get the project under the upload size limit:
* Project > Install Android Build Template...
* AssetLib > Godot OpenXR Vendors Plugin v2
